title: Quiz 2 — Solutions & Chemical Safety
revision: 2026-11 rev2 — 70:30 LOTS:HOTS, balanced choices, in-scope items only

questions.text: Which mixture is a SOLUTION?
options: Vinegar
Muddy water
Halo-halo
Sand and gravel
questions.correct: Vinegar

questions.text: In salt water, which substance is the solute?
options: Salt
Water
Both salt and water
Neither of them
questions.correct: Salt

questions.text: Why is water called the universal solvent?
options: It dissolves more substances than any other liquid
It is the only liquid that is found on the whole planet
It never dissolves anything that is a solid
It turns every solute it touches into a gas
questions.correct: It dissolves more substances than any other liquid

questions.text: Which describes a SATURATED solution?
options: No more solute can dissolve at that temperature
It has no solute dissolved in it at all yet
It can still dissolve a very large amount of solute
Its solute has completely evaporated already
questions.correct: No more solute can dissolve at that temperature

questions.text: Why does a softdrink fizz more when opened warm than when opened cold?
options: Gases are less soluble in warm liquids
Warm liquids hold more gas than cold ones
Cold drinks have no carbon dioxide inside
Sugar reacts with heat to make more bubbles
questions.correct: Gases are less soluble in warm liquids

questions.text: Which is a SOLID-in-SOLID solution?
options: Brass
Air
Soda
Brine
questions.correct: Brass

questions.text: Why do plants wilt in very salty soil?
options: Water moves out of the roots by osmosis
Salt fills the leaves and blocks the sunlight
Salt makes the roots take in too much water
Salt reacts with chlorophyll and burns the leaves
questions.correct: Water moves out of the roots by osmosis

questions.text: A 250 mL bottle of mouthwash is 20% alcohol by volume. How much alcohol does it contain?
options: 50 mL
20 mL
125 mL
230 mL
questions.correct: 50 mL

questions.text: In an experiment on salt and monggo growth, a student waters each group a different amount AND uses different salt levels. What is wrong?
options: Two variables changed, so the cause is unclear
Monggo seeds cannot grow in plain water at all
The salt levels should all be exactly the same
Seedling height cannot be measured with a ruler
questions.correct: Two variables changed, so the cause is unclear

questions.text: Two rivers have the same pollution, but one receives hot factory water. Which river is MORE likely to have fish kills, and why?
options: The warm one — it holds less dissolved oxygen
The cool one — cold water holds no oxygen at all
The warm one — warm water has more oxygen in it
Both equally — temperature has no effect on oxygen
questions.correct: The warm one — it holds less dissolved oxygen

questions.text: What does the GHS flame pictogram warn about?
options: The product catches fire easily
The product is toxic to aquatic life
The product corrodes skin and metals
The product is a gas under pressure
questions.correct: The product catches fire easily

questions.text: Why should chemicals never be stored in softdrink bottles?
options: Someone, especially a child, may drink them
The plastic makes chemicals much stronger
Softdrink bottles are too small for them
The chemicals will turn into soda over time
questions.correct: Someone, especially a child, may drink them

questions.text: Why should acid be added to water and not water to acid?
options: Water absorbs the heat, preventing splashing
Acid floats on top of water and cannot mix with it
Water added to acid makes the acid weaker
It saves time when diluting large amounts
questions.correct: Water absorbs the heat, preventing splashing

questions.text: What is eutrophication?
options: Nutrient pollution causing algal blooms and oxygen loss
Water becoming much cleaner after detergent is added to it
Fish multiplying quickly because of extra phosphates
Rivers drying up because of chemical evaporation
questions.correct: Nutrient pollution causing algal blooms and oxygen loss

questions.text: Which signal word on a label means the MORE severe hazard?
options: DANGER
WARNING
NOTICE
REMINDER
questions.correct: DANGER

questions.text: What does RA 6969 regulate?
options: Toxic substances and hazardous wastes
Clean air and vehicle emissions
Solid waste and household garbage segregation
Wildlife and protected forests
questions.correct: Toxic substances and hazardous wastes

questions.text: Why must toxic metals like mercury be kept out of rivers?
options: They build up in organisms along the food chain
They make the river water much colder during the night
They break down quickly into harmless sugars
They help fish grow larger and multiply faster
questions.correct: They build up in organisms along the food chain

questions.text: A family has used motor oil, expired pesticide and old batteries. What should they do?
options: Bring them to a hazardous-waste collection point
Pour the oil and pesticide down the kitchen sink
Bury all of them together in the vegetable garden
Burn them in an open pit far from the house
questions.correct: Bring them to a hazardous-waste collection point

questions.text: A barangay must choose ONE action to reduce fish kills caused by laundry wastewater in a creek. Which is BEST?
options: Promote phosphate-free detergents and proper drainage
Add more salt to the creek to kill all of the growing algae
Ask everyone to use twice the usual detergent amount
Remove the fish from the creek so none of them die
questions.correct: Promote phosphate-free detergents and proper drainage

questions.text: Students must design a chemical storage plan for the school canteen. Which plan is MOST complete?
options: Labeled containers, grouped by hazard, locked, away from food
One open shelf for all chemicals, placed near the food
Chemicals in reused juice bottles so the staff can easily see levels
Chemicals kept in the cooler with drinks to stay fresh
questions.correct: Labeled containers, grouped by hazard, locked, away from food
